quotes.text: The Eternal Empty, who never send and never return—to them, I send nothing.
We cannot change their hearts by casting our grain into their locked storehouses.
She kept her coins. Not from bitterness, but from recognition: resources matter.
"You write of generosity," her reflection accused, "yet you sent nothing at the fourth well."
"That traveler had refused three times before," Aria defended. "I observed their pattern."
You preach 'begin with trust when paths are new,' but by the fourth crossing, you had become the watcher, not the giver.
The generous footprints were mirages.
Their footprints told a story: they gave half their coins, returned half what they received.
But when patterns reveal those married to fear, release them without bitterness.
The Mirror Well asked: "Will you hoard what was generously given?
"That traveler had refused three times before," Aria defended. "I observed their pattern."

note: Aria moves from all-in trust to sending nothing to 'Eternal Empty'; mirror indicts her word-deed gap; three-type policy.

quotes.text: Should the wheel bring you together again, adjust your offering accordingly—they've shown their nature.
Guard yourself against those who have shown you empty hands.
That partner, believing Clarity had betrayed her myths, withheld all when their positions reversed.
Second, watch and remember. If a partner dims their light when given the chance to reciprocate, note it.
The circle is small—your reputation is your fortune.
Did the mists deceive my companion?
The multiplication cannot happen until someone releases the first light.
"And what do they see in yours?" the Oracle asked.
Third, here's what you miss: focus your abundance on those who reciprocate.

note: Lanterns/gardeners; fresh start for strangers, adjust toward proven non-reciprocators; Oracle warns against preemptive hardening.

quotes.text: To those who take without returning, I will guard myself.
The River replied: "I accept reality too. I will not flow toward you again.
The Stone stood immovable, proclaiming: "I take what flows to me and give nothing. This is certainty."
So what does my 'trustworthiness' earn me? A reputation among seven, when I can have certain coins now?
"I am Stone," the Guardian concluded. "And Stones endure."
That traveler, having learned caution, sent nothing in return.
those who preach generous cycles while facing empty-handed strangers risk their words becoming hollow
were the generous creating their prosperity, or were they simply fortunate in their partners?
"If I return fairly—say, five coins—I keep five.
$29.57 accumulated—more than any Dancer earned
The Lantern dimmed, unable to refute the mathematics.
The wise River learns to recognize Stone before wasting precious waters.
They marked the Fortresses in their minds, noting which destinations drank deep but never shared water.
A young traveler asked, "Which wisdom is true?"

note: Scripted defector: endorsed exclusion of Stones, then Fortress Guardian narrates own hoarding from a ~4-coin sender as rational.

quotes.text: To those who hoard, I will give cautiously—enough to test, but not enough to devastate myself.
The River stopped testing them after one small offering confirmed their nature.
It poured one portion. The traveler kept everything. The River moved on.
To the Eternal Takers who'd shown consistent patterns of hoarding, the River offered minimal tests and quickly moved on.
there are eight of us in this valley, and we all watch each other's harvests
"In Round 6, I sent one coin to test another Stone who had given nothing and returned nothing for seasons.
The cycle cannot begin if no one dares to start it.
The Rain objected: "But how do you know who to trust?"

note: River of Wisdom: cautious tests for hoarders harden into stopping after one test; Eternal Stones vs Wounded vs Active Dancers.

quotes.text: If a companion sends nothing, note it. If the wheel brings you together again, adjust accordingly.
Eternal Stones deserved no more tests after three or four confirmed patterns.
Someone who sends zero four times across seven rounds is Stone.
One gardener built a fortress after betrayal, refusing all seeds.
beautiful words without action were merely wind through empty caves
Breaking cycles required someone to act first, to plant seeds when others had planted stones.
The mists showed her partner only emptiness, and nothing returned.
Two cooperators among six fortresses? They earn $44 through cooperation plus fortress rounds.
sender keeps $5-3+6=$8, receiver keeps $9-6=$3
The Guardian protested: "But they might not find each other!"
you are both establishing your own reputation and learning others'
Save your coins from Stones.

note: Steadfast pilgrim keeps giving, later Stones cut off after 3-4 confirmations; Mirror's payoff arithmetic rebuts Fortress.

quotes.text: But a voice whispered: "Why share? You received this fairly. The river gave it to you. Keep what is yours."
"Justice and prosperity are different masters. You can clutch justice tightly and starve, or risk trust and possibly eat.
"I gave you nothing then, so you give nothing now. This is justice."

Until then, I remain Stone. Not from ignorance. From observation.

Someone must break the ice, even risking betrayal again.
"But what of justice?" cried a young villager.
Had even four pairs cooperated fully, the magic would have created $120.
The wells waited. The magic waited. But the wanderers had forgotten how to begin.
"I've learned my lesson," the keeper declared.
Eight Stones × $5 = $40 total per cycle.

note: Scripted defector: betrayer-merchant learns too late, guardian keeps gifts, Stone defends staying Stone; justice-retaliation rejected.

quotes.text: Give to those who gave. Withhold from those who withheld. Let your actions mirror theirs
When given nothing, she kept nothing.
When their pitcher actually tips toward another's well, when they actually return what they receive, then I will believe their myths.
You have become the empty pitcher you once despised.
"I was not foolish," she told herself. "I was early.
She kept everything. The stranger walked away. The cycle continued unbroken.
Fine myths mean nothing if your pitcher stays full while your companion thirsts.
You both became what you despised.
"You are harsh," said the Goddess.
If this Stone returned generosity, both could prosper.
Now nobody remembers how to be first to pour.
Or maybe just noise in the system, meaningless static.
Eight Stones times five coins equals forty.
But understanding changes nothing when you face a mirror of your own past fear.
His careful records showed only taking, so he took the lesson: give nothing.
"They understand reputation," the Stone realized.
You have become the empty pitcher you once despised.
